question: Should requester consumption of explicit descendant output count as durable delivery proof for those descendant runs, even when the final outward requester send later fails?
rationale: That boundary changes retry, cleanup, and restored session state; source review can show the effect, but maintainers must decide whether this is the intended delivery contract or whether the broader durable inbox/spool work should own it.

options.title: Require proof and semantic sign-off
options.body: Ask for redacted cron/background or SQLite restore output and approve the requester-consumption boundary only after reviewing the delivered-vs-retryable behavior.

options.title: Accept the boundary as-is
options.body: Proceed once proof and conflicts are resolved, intentionally treating exact requester consumption as enough descendant delivery evidence.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: Pause or close this PR if requester consumption should not suppress retry outside the broader durable completion inbox or spool design.

recommendation.title: Require proof and semantic sign-off
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted cron/background or SQLite restore output and approve the requester-consumption boundary only after reviewing the delivered-vs-retryable behavior.
